pr_title: Added option to enable delayed socket operations
pr_body:
- There's performance overhead ~8-10% in wrapping the IDuplex pipe without the delayed start and more overhead in adding the delayed start on top of that.
- This makes the feature opt-in for those that want to do more complex things with the socket.

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/34611

Numbers for plaintext:

Scenario (but I ran with my local changes):
```
crank --config https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aspnet/Benchmarks/main/scenarios/plaintext.benchmarks.yml --scenario plaintext --profile aspnet-citrine-amd --application.channel edge --application.framework net6.0 
```

- When I ran with the changes in main: 6,019,780
- When I reverted the change:   7,376,255 
- Just wrapping the Transport without delayed reads/writes: 6,611,234
- This PR: 7,061,812

~PS: I'm not 100% sure where the ~370K RPS is gone (I need to do a little digging to see what additional overhead this PR adds, it shouldn't be any).~
- Removed EnsureStarted from DisposeAsync : 7,220,432
- Removed Task.Run from EnsureStarted: 7,162,644
- Removed Task.Run from EnsureStarted and removed EnsureStarted from DisposeAsync: 7,403,048

🤔
pr_comments:
Thank you for submitting this for API review. This will be reviewed by @dotnet/aspnet-api-review at the next meeting of the ASP.NET Core API Review group. Please ensure you take a look at [the API review process documentation](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/master/docs/APIReviewProcess.md) and ensure that:

* The PR contains changes to the reference-assembly that describe the API change. **Or**, you have included a snippet of reference-assembly-style code that illustrates the API change.
* The PR describes the impact to users, both positive (useful new APIs) and negative (breaking changes).
* Someone is assigned to "champion" this change in the meeting, and they understand the impact and design of the change.
This change looks fine to me, but I'd like to better understand the perf deltas.

Interesting that wrapping was only half the regression. I figured that'd account for nearly all of it on our benchmarks that reuse connections like plaintext. I thought a single extra non-volatile (most of the time) check per read-write would be relatively inexpensive even though it's a super hot path.

> Removed EnsureStarted from DisposeAsync : 7,220,432
> Removed Task.Run from EnsureStarted: 7,162,644
> Removed Task.Run from EnsureStarted and removed EnsureStarted from DisposeAsync: 7,403,048

How could changing the connection dispose path possibly impact perf on these benchmarks? These tests only close connections after the benchmark completes, right?

The Task.Run thing also seems weird to me since that's just happening at the start of the connection. Is it just a first request slowdown causing a huge difference in numbers? I guess that this only accounts for 100k RPS. Was that consistent?
API approved with a rename to the property name: `DelaySocketOptions` -> `DelaySocketOperations`
We're going to revert this change.
